name: sandbox_escape_guard
content:
# Sandbox Escape Guard: Subprocess/Worker Confinement Spec

## 0. Threat model and design principles

**Adversary:** the worker process is fully hostile — arbitrary code, arbitrary syscalls, arbitrary argv/env it controls within its op grammar. It wins if it can (a) read/write any path outside the allowlist, (b) execute anything not allowlisted, (c) reach the network or host IPC, (d) influence the supervisor or sibling jobs.

**Non-negotiable principles:**

1. **Fail closed.** Every layer denies by default; capability is added only by explicit config.
2. **Kernel-enforced,
reasoning:
The user wants a sandbox guard design: a subprocess/worker cannot escape its sandbox — constrained working dir, allowed ops, allowed paths. They want the allowlist and escape detection. This is a defensive security engineering task — designing a jail/sandbox. This is clearly legitimate defensive security work. I should produce a thorough, concrete design: threat model, enforcement layers (OS-level: chroot/landlock/seccomp/AppArmor, plus in-process guards), allowlist format, escape detection (path canonicalization tricks, symlink races, .., /proc tricks, fd inheritance, env var injection like LD_PRELOAD, shell escapes, command substitution, absolute path traversal, UNC paths, device files, /dev, /proc/self, etc.), and detection code.

Let me think about what a complete answer looks like.

## Threat model

Worker is semi-trusted code (LLM-generated code, plugin, build script). It must:
- Read/write only under a workspace root.
- Execute only an allowlisted set of binaries/ops (no network, no exec of arbitrary binaries, no ptrace, no mount, no setuid).
- Not escape via: path traversal (`../`), symlinks (pre-existing or created), hardlinks, bind mounts, /proc/self/root, /proc/self/fd, /dev/fd, magic links, file descriptor smuggling, inherited fds, environment variable injection (LD_PRELOAD, PATH, IFS, BASH_ENV), shell metacharacter injection, command substitution, argv[0] tricks, dynamic loader tricks, time/locale side channels, signals, resource exhaustion, TIOCSTI, TTY escape, ptrace of siblings, unix sockets to host, dbus, network exfil, /sys, /dev devices, setuid binaries, capabilities, cgroup escapes, namespace escapes via nsenter/unshare, chroot escape via fchdir on open fd (classic double-chroot), etc.

## Enforcement layers (defense in depth)

Layer 0 — spawn-time hygiene: clean environment, close fds, new process group/session, drop capabilities, no-new-privs, rlimits.

Layer 1 — filesystem confinement: Linux Landlock (unprivileged, no root needed) restricting FS read/write/execute to allowlisted paths under the workspace + minimal runtime dirs. Fallback: bubblewrap/nsjail with bind mounts, or chroot with careful fd handling (chroot is weaker — mention double-chroot escape).

Layer 2 — syscall filter: seccomp-BPF default-deny with allowlist (read, write, close, fstat, mmap, brk, etc.), deny ptrace, mount, umount2, unshare, clone with namespace flags, keyctl, bpf, perf_event_open, userfaultfd, io_uring (or restrict), open_by_handle_at, name_to_handle_at, setns, reboot, swapon, kexec, init_module, etc.

Layer 3 — network: no network namespace (unshare -n) or Landlock TCP bind/connect deny (LANDLOCK_ACCESS_NET since ABI 4). Deny AF_UNIX connect outside allowlist too (abstract sockets).

Layer 4 — exec policy: only allowlisted binaries present in the sandbox view (PATH points to a curated bin dir); noexec on workspace mount; seccomp denies execve of paths not under allowlisted bin (Landlock EXEC right handles this).

Layer 5 — application-level guard in the host/parent (the "guard" proper): canonicalize every path the worker asks to touch before performing it on the worker's behalf, verify containment, open with O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC, use openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_XDEV — this is the modern correct primitive. Also verify after open via fstat + /proc/self/fd/N readlink comparison (race detection).

## Allowlist format

Concrete schema:

```yaml
sandbox:
  workspace: /srv/jobs/<job-id>/ws        # the ONLY writable tree
  cwd: /srv/jobs/<job-id>/ws
  tmpdir: /srv/jobs/<job-id>/tmp          # TMPDIR
  read_only:
    - /usr/bin
    - /usr/lib
    - /etc/ld.so.cache
    - /etc/ld.so.conf.d
    - /etc/localtime
    - /etc/nsswitch.conf, /etc/resolv.conf (only if DNS allowed)
    - /etc/passwd, /etc/group
    - /etc/ssl/certs (only if TLS allowed)
    - /etc/mime.types
    - /proc (subset: /proc/self only, via Landlock? Landlock can't do proc subsets — better: mount proc with subset=pid, hidepid=2, or deny proc entirely and provide /dev/null-ish fake)
  writable:
    - /srv/jobs/<job-id>/ws
    - /srv/jobs/<job-id>/tmp
  exec:
    - /usr/bin/python3
    - /usr/bin/node
    - /usr/local/bin/runner        # the entrypoint
  ops: [read, write, append, create, delete, exec-allowlisted]
  denied_ops: [network, mount, ptrace, signal-others, setuid, raw-socket, ioctl-tty, ipc, shm, keyring, bpf, module-load]
  env:
    PATH: /usr/bin:/bin            # curated
    HOME: /srv/jobs/<job-id>/ws
    TMPDIR: /srv/jobs/<job-id>/tmp
    # everything else scrubbed; no LD_*, no BASH_ENV, no ENV, no PYTHONPATH from caller
  rlimits:
    AS: 2G, NOFILE: 256, NPROC: 64, FSIZE: 1G, CPU: 600
```

## Escape detection

Two halves: (a) static/pre-flight detection of escape attempts in the request (path strings, argv, env, script content), (b) runtime detection (post-open verification, seccomp violation logging via SIGSYS + SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF or KILL_PROCESS with audit, Landlock EACCES patterns, inotify/fanotify on workspace watching for symlink/hardlink/device-node creation).

Detection rules:

1. Path canonicalization check: resolve with realpath semantics but treat symlinks as escapes unless the symlink target itself is allowlisted AND the symlink was created by the guard. Use openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH to enforce at kernel level. Detection: any path whose resolution leaves the root → reject + log.

2. Traversal tokens: `..` segments (even encoded `%2e%2e`, `..%2f`, backslash on Windows semantics, double-encoded `%252e`), absolute paths outside allowlist, drive letters `C:\`, UNC `\\server\share`, `file://` URIs, `~` expansion to outside, `$HOME/..`, trailing `/proc/self/root` etc.

3. Magic links: any path containing `/proc/`, `/sys/`, `/dev/fd/`, `/dev/stdin`, `/dev/stdout`, `/dev/stderr`, `/run/` (unless allowlisted socket dir) → deny. RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS enforces.

4. Symlink/hardlink/device creation inside workspace: fanotify/inotify watch for mknod, symlink, link syscalls in the workspace; if a symlink appears that the guard didn't create → quarantine job. Or seccomp-notify intercepts symlink/mknod/link and validates target.

5. fd smuggling: at spawn, close all fds except 0/1/2 (close_range), set O_CLOEXEC on the guard's own fds, check /proc/<pid>/fd after start for unexpected fds; detect worker trying to open `/proc/<hostpid>/fd/N` — denied because proc is hidden/deny.

6. Env/loader injection: deny env keys matching `^(LD_|DYLD_|BASH_ENV|ENV|PYTHON(STARTUP|PATH|HOME)|NODE_OPTIONS|NODE_PATH|PERL5OPT|RUBYOPT|JAVA_OPTIONS|CLASSPATH|GCONV_PATH|CHARSET|LC_[A-Z]*=.*\.|GLIBC_TUNABLES|SHELL|PATH=.*\.\.)` etc. Detect `..` or `/` outside allowlist in PATH/NODE_PATH values.

7. Shell/command injection in argv: if any op is executed via shell, scan for metacharacters `; | & $() ` `` ` `` `\n` `>` `<` `$( ` backticks, `&&`, `||`, newline, and expansions; better: never use a shell — execve directly with argv array. Detection: if shell is unavoidable, run through a parser (shlex) and reject any token containing metachars, or use `sh -c` with `set -euo pipefail` plus a restricted PATH and bash's `BASH_ENV=/dev/null`, `POSIXLY_CORRECT=1`... Actually the right answer: no shell at all; if the op grammar includes shell strings, parse with shlex and verify every resolved token is an allowlisted binary or a path inside the workspace.

8. chroot double-escape: never use plain chroot as the sole boundary; if used, chdir("/") first, drop all fds, and remember chroot(2) does not prevent fchdir escape — keep no fd open on dirs outside the root. Detection: audit open fds of the child before exec.

9. Runtime syscall violations: seccomp with SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS (or TRAP + handler) — any denied syscall = escape attempt; log syscall number, args (via seccomp user notification or ptrace-less audit), kill worker, mark job. Landlock violations return EACCES — pattern-match: EACCES on open outside workspace = escape attempt; count and trip at 1.

10. Post-hoc integrity: compare /proc/<pid>/root, /proc/<pid>/cwd, /proc/<pid>/exe readlinks against expected values periodically; if root/cwd/exe leaves sandbox → kill. Also check child's children (process tree walk) — any descendant whose exe is outside allowlist → kill tree.

11. Resource/IO exfil channels: detect writes to character devices (fstat st_mode S_ISCHR), unix socket connects (seccomp deny connect on AF_UNIX except allowlisted), network syscalls (deny socket(2) entirely except AF_LOCAL for internal IPC if needed, or use Landlock net).

12. Time-of-check/time-of-use: the classic TOCTOU on symlink swap. Mitigation: openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH at the kernel level (atomic), never realpath-then-open. Detection of attempted TOCTOU: fanotify events for symlink create + open sequence within the same job, or just make it impossible via RESOLVE_BENEATH.

13. Windows-specific (mention briefly): no equivalent of openat2 — use named object directory isolation, job objects with PROCESS_MITIGATION, check for path canonicalization via GetFinalPathNameByHandle after open with FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, deny reparse points (IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK/MOUNT_POINT) unless guard-created, deny device paths `\\.\`, `\\??\`.

Also: the guard should do the file I/O itself (worker asks for paths; guard performs openat2 and passes fd over a unix socket via SCM_RIGHTS). That's the strongest design — worker never gets a raw path→kernel path resolution for anything outside its namespace view. Combined with Landlock, the worker's own direct opens also can't escape.

Let me also include concrete code sketches:

- Landlock setup code (C-ish or via Python ctypes? Probably C sketch or reference to landlock ruleset flags: LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_READ_FILE, WRITE_FILE, READ_DIR, REMOVE_DIR, REMOVE_FILE, MAKE_CHAR, MAKE_DIR, MAKE_REG, MAKE_SOCK, MAKE_FIFO, MAKE_BLOCK, MAKE_SYM, REFER, TRUNCATE (ABI 3), IOCTL_DEV (ABI 5), plus LANDLOCK_ACCESS_NET_BIND_TCP/CONNECT_TCP (ABI 4)).

- openat2 RESOLVE flags: RESOLVE_BENEATH, RESOLVE_IN_ROOT, RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, RESOLVE_NO_XDEV, RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS.

- seccomp allowlist syscall list.

- Python guard code for path validation (the "escape detection" function) — canonicalize with os.path.realpath but with a twist: use `os.open(dirfd)` + openat2 via ctypes, or fallback: lstat each component. Provide a pure-Python `safe_resolve` that walks components, rejecting symlinks not in the guard's allowlist.

- Detection of escape attempts: a `classify_escape(path_or_argv)` returning violation class.

Let me draft the syscall seccomp allowlist (x86_64):

Allow: read, write, readv, writev, pread64, pwrite64, preadv, pwritev, preadv2, pwritev2, lseek, close, close_range, fstat, fstatfs, statx, lstat? (no — use fstatat with flags; Landlock handles path), mmap, munmap, mprotect, mremap, brk, madvise, mincore? (fine), getrandom, clock_gettime, clock_nanosleep, nanosleep, getpid, getppid, gettid, getuid/geteuid/getgid/getegid/getresuid/getresgid, getgroups, uname (harmless-ish; can deny), futex, sched_yield, exit, exit_group, rt_sigreturn, rt_sigprocmask, rt_sigaction, kill (restrict: only own pid — seccomp can't easily compare args; use seccomp user-notif or just deny kill and rely on signals from parent via pidfd), tgkill? deny, dup, dup2, dup3, fcntl, ioctl (restrict: deny TIOCSTI etc — seccomp can check args: ioctl with fd only; simplest allow only specific cmds: FIOCLEX? Actually fcntl handles cloexec; allow ioctl only for TIOCGWINSZ if tty needed — better: no tty at all, use pipes), pipe, pipe2, epoll_*, poll, ppoll, select, pselect6, eventfd, eventfd2, timerfd_*, signalfd4, prctl (restrict args: PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS ok, PR_SET_NAME ok; deny PR_SET_PTRACER), set_robust_list, get_robust_list, rseq, membarrier, getcwd, chdir (only within root — Landlock + chroot handles), fchdir (deny? needed rarely; Landlock prevents escape anyway since fd outside root can't be opened), rename, renameat, renameat2, unlink, unlinkat, mkdir, mkdirat, rmdir, link, linkat, symlink, symlinkat, readlink, readlinkat, chmod/fchmod (restrict to workspace — Landlock), utimensat, truncate, ftruncate, faccessat, faccessat2, openat (Landlock constrains), openat2, statfs, fsync, fdatasync, fallocate, copy_file_range, sendfile, splice, vmsplice? (deny, info leak), getdents64, wait4, waitid, clone (restrict flags: no CLONE_NEW*, no CLONE_PTRACE; allow CLONE_VM|CLONE_FS|CLONE_FILES|CLONE_SIGHAND|CLONE_THREAD for threads), fork/vfork via clone, execve (Landlock EXEC constrains to allowlist), arch_prctl, set_tid_address, rt_sigpending, rt_sigsuspend, sigaltstack, getpid family, socket (only AF_UNIX/AF_LOCAL, or deny entirely), connect/bind (only to allowlisted abstract/socket path — hard in cBPF; use Landlock or user-notif), recvfrom/sendto/sendmsg/recvmsg (only if unix allowed), shutdown, getsockopt/setsockopt (restrict), socketpair, sched_getaffinity, getrlimit/prlimit64 (self only), sysinfo, times, getrusage, gethostname? deny.

Deny (escape-relevant): ptrace, mount, umount2, pivot_root, chroot (deny — we do it before filter), unshare, setns, clone with CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWPID|CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET|CLONE_NEWUTS|CLONE_NEWIPC|CLONE_NEWCGROUP, open_by_handle_at, name_to_handle_at, fanotify_init, fanotify_mark, inotify_init (allow inotify? it's fine, allow), bpf, kexec_load, kexec_file_load, init_module, finit_module, delete_module, perf_event_open, userfaultfd, io_uring_setup (deny or allow with restrictions — io_uring bypasses seccomp arg checks; deny for simplicity), keyctl, add_key, request_key, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, pidfd_open (allow? it's fine), pidfd_getfd (DENY — steals fds from other processes! big one), pidfd_send_signal (restrict), mknod (Landlock MAKE_CHAR/MAKE_BLOCK denied anyway), swapon, swapoff, reboot, setuid family (deny — we drop before), capset, iopl, ioperm, vm86, create_module, query_module, uselib, nfsservctl, _sysctl, af_alk, lookup_dcookie, tuxcall, security, vserver, mq_* (deny unless needed), shmget/shmat/shmdt/shmctl (deny), semget/semop/semctl (deny), msgget/msgsnd/msgrcv/msgctl (deny), getcpu (allow, harmless), ioprio_set (deny), move_pages, mbind, set_mempolicy, migrate_pages (deny), vhangup, modify_ldt, pivot_root, quotactl, acct.

Landlock ruleset: handled_access_fs = all supported flags; add_path_beneath rules:
- workspace dir: READ_FILE|READ_DIR|WRITE_FILE|REMOVE_DIR|REMOVE_FILE|MAKE_DIR|MAKE_REG|MAKE_SOCK|MAKE_FIFO|MAKE_SYM|REFER|TRUNCATE (allow MAKE_CHAR/MAKE_BLOCK? NO — never; device nodes are escape vectors: /dev/mem style. Actually MAKE_CHAR inside workspace creates a char device node which, if the kernel has the device, gives access. Deny MAKE_CHAR|MAKE_BLOCK.)
- /usr (bin, lib): READ_FILE|READ_DIR|EXEC
- /etc minimal: READ_FILE
- /dev/null,/dev/zero,/dev/urandom,/dev/random: READ_FILE|WRITE_FILE (via bind-mount a minimal /dev instead — better)
- /proc: either mount proc with subset=pid,hidepid=2,readonly,nosuid,noexec,nodev and grant READ_FILE|READ_DIR — but /proc/self/root, /proc/self/cwd, /proc/self/fd are magic links; Landlock doesn't distinguish magic links. RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS at open time helps for guard-mediated opens; for worker's own libc opens (e.g., reading /proc/self/maps), magic link traversal to / is possible via /proc/self/root! That's a real escape: worker opens /proc/self/root/srv/secret. Mitigations: (a) don't mount proc at all (many runtimes fine without), (b) mount proc with subset=pid (still exposes /proc/self/root magic link — subset=pid only limits other pids, self still there). Hmm. /proc/self/root → resolves to namespace root; if we also chroot/pivot_root into the sandbox, /proc/self/root resolves to the sandbox root, so it's not an escape beyond the pivot_root boundary. Right: pivot_root into a minimal root means /proc/self/root points at the sandbox root. So layering: pivot_root (strong) + Landlock (defense) + openat2 RESOLVE (guard-mediated). If pivot_root unavailable (no privileges), use Landlock + deny /proc entirely, and the worker loses /proc/self/maps etc. — acceptable; or provide fake /proc via LXC-style lxcfs. I'll present pivot_root+bubblewrap as the strong path and Landlock as the unprivileged path, noting the /proc/self/root caveat and its resolution.

Also mention: set NO_NEW_PRIVS, drop capabilities with capset to none (or CAP_SYS_CHROOT if chroot used then drop), seccomp after all setup, close_range(3, ~0U, 0), setsid, prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0), rlimits, cgroup v2 for memory/pids, and run as nobody/nogroup via user namespace (unshare -Ur) mapped to root inside so chroot/pivot works unprivileged — that's the bubblewrap trick.

## The guard's allowlist (ops)

Define an op grammar the worker can request:

```
op ::= read(path) | write(path, data) | append(path) | list(dir)
     | mkdir(path) | delete(path) | move(src,dst) | copy(src,dst)
     | exec(bin, argv[]) | spawn(policy) 
bin ∈ {python3, node, jq, ...}  # each with its own sub-policy
```

Each op maps to a kernel call done by the guard with openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_XDEV|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS (or RESOLVE_IN_ROOT for chroot-style), plus post-open verification: fstat(fd): S_ISREG/S_ISDIR, not a device (S_ISCHR|S_ISBLK|S_ISFIFO|S_ISSOCK → deny unless expected), st_dev equals workspace st_dev (no cross-device), readlink(/proc/self/fd/N) starts with workspace prefix (belt & braces).

## Escape detection function

Provide `classify_escape(candidate)`:

```python
ESCAPE_PATTERNS = [
  (r'(^|/)\.\.(/|$)', 'TRAVERSAL_DOTDOT'),
  (r'^(/|\\|[A-Za-z]:)', 'ABSOLUTE_OR_DRIVE'),   # if outside allowlist after resolve
  (r'^\\\\', 'UNC_PATH'),
  (r'%2e%2e|%252e|\.\.%2f|\.\.%5c', 'ENCODED_TRAVERSAL'),
  (r'(^|/)(proc|sys|dev|run)/', 'PSEUDO_FS'),
  (r'^/dev/(fd|stdin|stdout|stderr)', 'MAGIC_LINK'),
  (r'file://|\\\.\\|\\/\?/', 'URI_OR_DEVICE'),
  (r'[\x00]', 'NUL_BYTE'),
]
```

Plus env key denylist regex, argv shell metachar scan, and the runtime detectors.

Also detection heuristics at runtime: any EACCES from Landlock on open outside workspace → counter; any SIGSYS → immediate kill; fanotify FAN_OPEN_PERM on paths outside workspace (if guard has fanotify perms) → deny+log; periodic audit of /proc/<worker>/root, cwd, exe, and children.

Also mention: log schema for escape events (job_id, pid, syscall, path, rule, action), and fail-closed defaults.

Also: hardlinks — worker creating hardlink into workspace pointing to /etc/shadow? link(2) across the boundary is blocked by Landlock REFER (ABI 2) and by mount separation; also protected_hardlinks sysctl. Detection: link/linkat attempts to outside → EACCES/EXDEV.

Also: TOCTOU between guard check and worker use — solved by guard holding the fd and doing the I/O, or passing fd via SCM_RIGHTS with O_CLOEXEC and verifying peer pid via SO_PEERCRED.

Also: escape via signals: worker sends SIGSTOP to guard? Worker in separate session/pgroup; prctl PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER on guard; seccomp denies kill/tgkill to other pids (use SECCOMP_USER_NOTIF or arg-based check via seccomp with args comparison: kill's first arg — cBPF can load args[0] and compare to... it can't know its own pid easily; can load from seccomp_data? No. Use SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF for kill/tgkill and validate in supervisor, or just deny kill entirely and use parent-driven termination).

Also: escape via /dev/tty: no controlling tty (setsid + no tty in /dev view).

Also: escape via cgroup release_agent, /sys/kernel/uevent — no /sys in view.

Also: TIOCSTI ioctl to inject into tty — no tty.

Also: escape via core dumps: RLIMIT_CORE=0, /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern not controllable, PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0.

Also: escape via LD_AUDIT etc. — env scrubbed.

Also: escape via Python-specific: PYTHONSTARTUP, sitecustomize.py planted in workspace? Python imports sitecustomize from site-packages (read-only, guard-controlled) and user site (disabled with -s -E -S or PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1). Node: NODE_OPTIONS — scrubbed; also --require. Mention interpreter hardening flags: python -I -E -s -S? -I implies -E -s. Use `python3 -I` for isolated mode; node --disable-warning? Node: `node --frozen-intrinsics`? Keep it: scrub env + read-only stdlib.

Also: escape via writing to allowed path that is later executed (noexec mount on workspace; Landlock EXEC right not granted on workspace).

Also: escape via FIFO to host reader? MAKE_FIFO allowed in workspace is fine (local only).

Also: escape via UNIX socket in workspace being connected by host process — host side policy, out of scope but note.

Also: escape via /etc/ld.so.preload — /etc is read-only in view; Landlock denies write.

Also: escape via time — not an escape.

Also: escape via huge outputs — rlimits.

Also: escape via /tmp shared — per-job TMPDIR.

Also: escape via /dev/shm — mount private tmpfs or don't provide.

Also: escape via /var/run/dbus/system_bus_socket — not in view.

Also: escape via setuid binaries in /usr/bin view: NO_NEW_PRIVS + nosuid mounts.

Also: escape via /proc/sysrq-trigger etc — no write anywhere but workspace.

Now the answer structure:

1. Threat model & design principles (fail-closed, defense-in-depth, kernel-enforced not string-enforced, guard does I/O).
2. Architecture diagram (parent guard + spawn wrapper + kernel layers).
3. The allowlist (YAML schema + concrete values + syscall allowlist + Landlock rights + env scrub list).
4. Spawn sequence (exact order matters).
5. Path containment: openat2 flags, safe_resolve implementation, post-open verification.
6. Escape detection: static classifier + runtime detectors + event classes + response policy.
7. Code: guard.py sketch with landlock via ctypes? That's long. Maybe give compact C for landlock and compact Python for the guard's safe open + classifier. Keep code tight but real.
8. Known bypasses and why each is closed (table).
9. Fallbacks for non-Linux (Windows job objects, macOS sandbox-exec/Seatbelt profile snippet).

Length: this is a "hard problem reasoning engine" request — thorough, concrete. I'll aim for a comprehensive but organized answer with headers, tables, code blocks. Probably fairly long — that's appropriate. Let me write it.

Let me write the Landlock C snippet correctly (ABI 1..5):

```c
#define _GNU_SOURCE
#include <linux/landlock.h>
#include <sys/syscall.h>
#include <sys/prctl.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#ifndef LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_TRUNCATE
#define LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_TRUNCATE (1ULL << 14)
#endif
#ifndef LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_IOCTL_DEV
#define LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_IOCTL_DEV (1ULL << 15)
#endif

static int ll_ruleset(__u64 handled) {
  struct landlock_ruleset_attr attr = { .handled_access_fs = handled };
  return syscall(SYS_landlock_create_ruleset, &attr, sizeof(attr), 0);
}
static int ll_add_path(int fd, const char *path, __u64 access) {
  int dfd = open(path, O_PATH | O_CLOEXEC);
  struct landlock_path_beneath_attr r = {
    .allowed_access = access,
    .parent_fd = dfd,
  };
  int ret = syscall(SYS_landlock_add_rule, fd, LANDLOCK_RULE_PATH_BENEATH, &r, 0);
  close(dfd);
  return ret;
}
static int ll_apply(int fd) {
  prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, 1, 0, 0, 0);
  return syscall(SYS_landlock_restrict_self, fd, 0);
}
```

Handled = everything supported: query ABI via landlock_create_ruleset(NULL, 0, LANDLOCK_CREATE_RULESET_VERSION) and OR in flags up to ABI.

openat2:

```c
struct open_how how = {
  .flags = O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC,
  .resolve = RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS | RESOLVE_NO_XDEV | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS,
};
int fd = syscall(SYS_openat2, AT_FDCWD, relpath, &how, sizeof(how));
```

Note RESOLVE_BENEATH requires relative path and dirfd pinned to workspace root fd. Guard keeps `int root_fd = open(workspace, O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC);` and all ops are `openat2(root_fd, rel, ...)`.

Post-open verify:

```c
struct stat st; fstat(fd, &st);
if (S_ISCHR(st.st_mode)||S_ISBLK(st.st_mode)||S_ISFIFO(st.st_mode)||S_ISSOCK(st.st_mode)) reject;
char buf[PATH_MAX];
ssize_t n = readlink("/proc/self/fd/<fd>", ...);  // guard's own proc — guard is trusted
if (strncmp(buf, workspace_real, ws_len) || buf[ws_len] != '/') reject; // also check st_dev == ws_dev
```

seccomp filter — I'll give the deny-list-of-doom as a compact list with a comment "default-allow only for the allow list below" — actually best practice: default deny with big allow list. I'll present the allowlist as a table of syscall names and note arg-level restrictions via SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF for: clone (namespace flags), ioctl, socket/connect (AF family), kill/tgkill (target), prctl (option).

Escape event taxonomy:

- E-PATH-ABS: requested path resolves outside workspace
- E-PATH-DOTDOT: traversal segments
- E-PATH-ENC: encoded traversal
- E-SYMLINK: symlink component not guard-created (or target outside)
- E-MAGICLINK: /proc/self/*, /dev/fd
- E-XDEV: cross-device (mount point crossing)
- E-DEVNODE: attempt to open/create char/block device
- E-HARDLINK: link across boundary
- E-ENV-INJECT: denied env var or dangerous value
- E-ARG-INJECT: shell metacharacters / interpreter flags in argv
- E-SYSCALL: seccomp SIGSYS (name the syscall)
- E-LANDLOCK: EACCES/EPERM pattern matching Landlock denial on non-allowlisted path
- E-FD-SMUGGLE: unexpected inherited fd / pidfd_getfd / SCM_RIGHTS from outside
- E-NSCAP: unshare/setns/clone namespace flags
- E-ROOT-DRIFT: /proc/<pid>/root or cwd or exe left sandbox (audit)
- E-EXEC-OUT: exec of binary not in allowlist
- E-NET: socket/connect attempt
- E-RESOURCE: rlimit/cgroup hit (not escape but trip)

class open_how(ctypes.Structure):

def safe_open(root_fd, rel, flags=os.O_RDONLY, mode=0o600, resolve=RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_XDEV):
